A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same GS-CLIP work, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. Both end with references on PDF page 10. Neither contains the appendices mentioned in Sections 4.1 and 4.4, so these judgments cover the supplied material, not unavailable supplementary content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on four datasets, multimodal comparisons, computational measurements and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark, multimodal, computational and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–6.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same two-stage method, geometry-aware prompts, GDDM, Depth-LoRA, synergistic refinement, anomaly scoring and losses. Visual inspection confirms that apparent equation differences from text extraction do not represent algorithm changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVTec3D-AD, Eyecandies, Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet under the same one-vs-rest and cross-dataset scenarios. Multimodal evaluation remains restricted to MVTec3D-AD and Eyecandies.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in each corresponding experiment in Tables 1–3, including CLIP, AA-CLIP, 3DzAL, MVP-PCLIP and PointAD where applicable. The newly cited DDE-CLIP is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same category-selection protocols, AUROC/AP/PRO metrics, ViT-L/14 backbone, image resolution, nine-view setup and 15/10-epoch training schedule. No experimental setting changes are documented in the supplied PDFs.

E4.justification: The supplied analyses are identical: component ablations in Table 4, GDDM parameter sensitivity in Figure 5, view-count sensitivity in Figure 6, qualitative comparisons in Figure 4 and computational analysis in Table 3. Additional appendix analyses are referenced but not included in either PDF.

E5.justification: Both retain averaging over three selected training categories for the one-vs-rest evaluation. Neither supplied PDF reports random-seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported numerical entries in Tables 1–4 and the findings displayed in Figures 4–6 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains GS-CLIP's MVTec3D-AD one-vs-rest scores of 83.6/96.5 for object-level metrics and 96.3/86.4 for point-level metrics.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(20) retain the same content. Changes in spacing and extractable equation text do not alter the rendered mathematics; neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about geometry-aware prompting, complementary rendered/depth representations and superior detection performance across four datasets.

C2.justification: Interpretations of modality complementarity, geometric prompting, cross-dataset generalization, parameter sensitivity and the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff are unchanged. The conclusion retains the same suggestion to explore native 3D representations and modal fusion.

D1.justification: The disclosed implementation details remain identical, including Open3D rendering, Adam, learning rates, LoRA rank 8, k=12 and an RTX 3090 GPU. The code-access statement and URL are unchanged. Appendix B is referenced for further details but absent from both supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 replaces the KANOCLIP citation, reference [16] in v1, with DDE-CLIP, reference [11] in v3. The surrounding discussion and research positioning remain unchanged; this is a limited substitution of cited work.

P1.justification: The prose and section organization are essentially unchanged. Limited editorial changes update the version/date stamp, renumber citations and revise author and publication-page information for the same PromptAD reference [18].

P2.justification: Figures 1–6 and Tables 1–4 retain their content, captions and placement. v3 removes printed page-number footers, adjusts some equation spacing, particularly on PDF page 5, and reflows the bibliography.

improvement.justification: The supplied v3 preserves the methods, experimental evidence, claims and reproducibility disclosures of v1. Its citation substitution, bibliographic edits and formatting adjustments do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss. The references to unavailable appendices remain unresolved in both PDFs.
